name: Alexander Gillon
bio: a Representative from South Carolina; born in Rotterdam, Holland, in 1741; pursued an academic course; immigrated to London, England, and engaged in commerce; in 1766 settled in Charleston, S.C., and established a large business; delegate to the Second Provincial Congress of South Carolina in 1775 and 1776; member of the first general assembly in 1776; served in the Revolutionary War; elected captain of the German Fusiliers of Charleston in May 1775; commodore of the South Carolina Navy in 1778 and sent to France to procure vessels; joined the fleet of Spanish vessels in the capture of the Bahama Islands, May 8, 1782; elected to the Confederation Congress in 1784, but did not attend; delegate to the South Carolina state convention which ratified the U.S. Constitution in 1788; elected as an Anti-Administration candidate to the Third Congress and served from March 4, 1793, until his death at his plantation, "Gillon's Retreat," Orangeburg District, S.C., October 6, 1794; interment in the family burial ground at "Gillon's Retreat," Calhoun County, S.C.
